subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following is formed by ionic bond?
solution: An ionic bond forms by transfer of electrons between a metal and a non-metal. Sodium is a metal and chlorine a non-metal, so \(\text{NaCl}\) is ionic, while \(\text{HCl}\), \(\text{NH}_3\) and \(\text{CH}_4\) are all covalent molecules of non-metals. Matches option C.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following has the highest melting point?
solution: Melting point of an ionic solid rises with lattice energy, which grows with the product of the ionic charges and with smaller ionic size. \(\text{MgO}\) is built from doubly charged \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\) and \(\text{O}^{2-}\), whereas the other three are singly charged pairs, so its lattice energy and melting point are far higher. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following has the greatest ionic character?
solution: Ionic character increases with the electronegativity difference between the two atoms, and by Fajans' rules a smaller, less polarizable anion keeps the bond more ionic. Fluorine is the most electronegative and smallest halogen, so \(\text{LiF}\) is the most ionic of the four lithium halides. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Dedup MAYBE vs bank 164da3b9 and e19faf5a (same Fajans-rule family) - kept as new: both bank rows ask the INVERSE question (maximum covalent character / lowest ionic character) over a different set of compounds.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: The formula of the compound formed between \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\) and \(\text{NO}_3^-\) is:
solution: The compound must be electrically neutral, so the total positive and negative charge have to cancel. One \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\) carries two positive charges and each \(\text{NO}_3^-\) carries one negative charge, so two nitrate ions are needed per magnesium ion, giving \(\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2\). Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following properties is shown by ionic compounds?
solution: As printed this question has no correct option. Ionic compounds have HIGH melting points, are GOOD conductors in solution, are soluble in polar solvents rather than organic ones, and ARE electrolytes - so every one of the four printed options states a property ionic compounds do NOT show. Option A is keyed only as a placeholder.
reviewNote: DEFECTIVE - no printed option is a true property of ionic compounds. All four options are the NEGATIONS of the correct properties (high melting point, good conductor in solution, soluble in polar solvents, electrolyte), which suggests the option block was inverted or belongs to a 'which is NOT shown' stem. Keyed (A) purely as a placeholder for OMR; the teacher must supply the intended key. Held PRIVATE.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following molecules is held together by covalent bonds?
solution: A covalent bond forms by sharing of electrons between non-metal atoms. Water is made of the non-metals hydrogen and oxygen sharing electron pairs, while \(\text{NaCl}\), \(\text{MgO}\) and \(\text{KBr}\) are all metal plus non-metal combinations and therefore ionic. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which molecule has a double covalent bond?
solution: Each oxygen atom has six valence electrons and needs two more to complete its octet, so the two atoms share two pairs of electrons and form a double bond. \(\text{Cl}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\) are single bonded and \(\text{N}_2\) is triple bonded. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: The bond formed by mutual sharing of one pair of electrons between two atoms is called:
solution: The number of shared electron pairs names the covalent bond: one shared pair is a single bond, two shared pairs a double bond and three a triple bond. Sharing exactly one pair therefore gives a single covalent bond, and an ionic bond involves transfer rather than sharing. Matches option A.

subtopic: Dipole Moment, Polarity and Intermolecular Forces
stem: Which of the following is a non-polar covalent molecule?
solution: A molecule is non-polar when its individual bond dipoles cancel by symmetry. Carbon dioxide is linear, so its two equal and opposite carbon-to-oxygen dipoles cancel and the net dipole moment is zero, whereas bent \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), pyramidal \(\text{NH}_3\) and diatomic \(\text{HCl}\) all have a resultant dipole. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Dedup MAYBE vs bank 88ba975a (zero dipole moment) - kept as new: different option set (that row offers HF, NH3, BF3, CHCl3) and it tests symmetry of a trigonal planar molecule rather than a linear one.

subtopic: Dipole Moment, Polarity and Intermolecular Forces
stem: Which of the following compounds has the lowest melting point?
solution: Melting point is set by the strength of the forces holding the solid together. \(\text{SiO}_2\) is a giant covalent network needing very high temperatures, water is held by hydrogen bonds and \(\text{P}_4\) is a molecular solid melting near 44 degrees Celsius, while \(\text{CO}_2\) is a non-polar molecular solid held only by weak dispersion forces and it sublimes at about minus 78 degrees Celsius. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following species is formed by coordinate bond?
solution: A coordinate bond is one in which both shared electrons come from the same atom. When \(\text{NH}_3\) bonds to \(\text{H}^+\) the nitrogen lone pair supplies both electrons, so the fourth bond in \(\text{NH}_4^+\) is coordinate; \(\text{Cl}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\) are ordinary covalent and \(\text{NaCl}\) is ionic. Matches option A.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: In \(\text{NH}_4^+\) ion, the coordinate bond is formed by the donation of lone pair from:
solution: Nitrogen in ammonia has three bonding pairs and one lone pair. That lone pair on nitrogen is donated to the electron-deficient \(\text{H}^+\) to create the fourth bond, and hydrogen has no lone pair to give. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following complexes contains coordinate bond?
solution: In a complex ion each ligand donates a lone pair to the central metal ion, which is a coordinate bond. In \([\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+\) two ammonia ligands each donate a nitrogen lone pair to the silver ion, whereas \(\text{NaCl}\) and \(\text{KBr}\) are simple ionic salts. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: A coordinate bond is represented by:
solution: A coordinate bond is drawn as an arrow pointing from the donor atom, which supplies both electrons, towards the acceptor atom. A plain dash denotes an ordinary single covalent bond, a double dash a double bond, and the paired arrows denote a reversible reaction. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which ligand donates a lone pair to the central atom through coordinate bond?
solution: A ligand must carry at least one lone pair to donate. Ammonia is the standard example, with one lone pair on nitrogen donated to the central atom. Note that water and chloride also carry lone pairs and act as ligands, so only \(\text{Na}^+\) - a cation with no available lone pair - is definitely not a ligand. Matches option A.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Lattice energy is defined as the energy released when:
optA: One mole of ionic solid is sublimed
optB: One mole of ionic solid is formed from its gaseous ions
optC: One mole of cations in solution is hydrated
optD: One mole of ionic solid is melted
solution: Lattice energy is the energy released when one mole of an ionic crystal is formed from its constituent ions in the gaseous state. Option C describes hydration enthalpy, while sublimation and melting describe breaking the lattice rather than forming it. Matches option B.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which of the following has the highest lattice energy?
solution: For ions of equal charge, lattice energy increases as the ions get smaller because the inter-ionic distance shrinks. \(\text{Li}^+\) and \(\text{F}^-\) are the smallest cation and anion among the four compounds, so \(\text{LiF}\) has the shortest inter-ionic distance and the highest lattice energy. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Dedup MAYBE vs bank 0a9420b6 (high lattice enthalpy) - kept as new: that row offers LiCl, NaCl, BeF2, CaCl2 and turns on ionic CHARGE, whereas this one is a pure ionic-SIZE comparison across four singly charged salts.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Which factor does NOT increase lattice energy?
solution: Lattice energy is directly proportional to the product of the ionic charges and inversely proportional to the distance between the ion centres. Raising the charge or shrinking the ions therefore raises it, while increasing the inter-ionic distance lowers it. Matches option C.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: In Born-Haber cycle, lattice energy is represented by:
solution: In the Born-Haber cycle each step carries its own enthalpy label, and the lattice formation step is written as \(\Delta H_{\text{latt}}\). The symbol \(\Delta H_f\) denotes the overall enthalpy of formation of the compound, not the lattice step. Matches option C.

subtopic: Ionic and Covalent Bonding, Lewis Structures and Octet Rule
stem: Lattice energy of an ionic compound is related to its melting point. The correct relation is:
optC: Lattice energy is independent of melting point
solution: A higher lattice energy means the ions are held together more strongly, so more thermal energy is needed to break the lattice apart. Melting point therefore rises as lattice energy rises, a direct proportionality. Matches option A.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: According to VBT, covalent bond is formed by:
solution: Valence Bond Theory describes a covalent bond as the overlap of two half-filled atomic orbitals, which pairs and shares their electrons between the two nuclei. Transfer of electrons gives an ionic bond and donation of a lone pair gives a coordinate bond. Matches option B.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: In \(\text{CH}_4\) molecule, carbon is:
solution: Carbon in methane is surrounded by four bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so four orbitals must be mixed. One \(2s\) and three \(2p\) orbitals combine to give four equivalent \(sp^3\) hybrid orbitals directed to the corners of a tetrahedron. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Dedup MAYBE vs bank 1e79e75c - kept as new: that row asks for hybridisation AND geometry as a paired answer, while this asks only for the hybridisation, over a different option set.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: Which of the following has the shape predicted by \(sp^2\) hybridisation?
solution: Boron in \(\text{BF}_3\) has three bonding pairs and no lone pair, so three orbitals mix to give \(sp^2\) hybridisation and a trigonal planar shape with bond angles of 120 degrees. Methane is \(sp^3\), ammonia is \(sp^3\) with a lone pair, and \(\text{BeCl}_2\) is \(sp\) and linear. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Dedup MAYBE vs bank 07f33cb1 - kept as new: that row asks which hybridisation gives trigonal geometry (options are hybridisation types), this asks which MOLECULE shows the sp2 shape.

subtopic: VSEPR Theory and Molecular Geometry
stem: The shape of \(\text{NH}_3\) molecule according to VBT is:
solution: Nitrogen in ammonia has three bonding pairs and one lone pair, giving four electron domains and \(sp^3\) hybridisation, so the electron geometry is tetrahedral. Because one corner is occupied by the lone pair, the shape described by the atom positions is trigonal pyramidal. Matches option D.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: In \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) molecule, the hybridisation of oxygen is:
solution: Oxygen in water has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, which is four electron domains in total. Four domains require four hybrid orbitals, so the oxygen is \(sp^3\) hybridised and the molecule is bent. Matches option C.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: The \(\sigma\) bond in \(\text{H}_2\) molecule is formed by:
solution: Each hydrogen atom has a single electron in its \(1s\) orbital and no \(p\) electrons. The bond therefore comes from head-on overlap of the two \(1s\) orbitals, an \(s-s\) overlap which gives a \(\sigma\) bond. Matches option A.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: The \(\sigma\) bond in \(\text{HCl}\) molecule is formed by:
solution: Hydrogen contributes a half-filled \(1s\) orbital while chlorine contributes a half-filled \(3p\) orbital. Head-on overlap of an \(s\) orbital with a \(p\) orbital gives the \(\sigma\) bond, so the overlap is \(s-p\). Matches option B.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: The \(\pi\) bond in ethene \((\text{C}_2\text{H}_4)\) is formed by:
solution: Each carbon in ethene is \(sp^2\) hybridised and keeps one unhybridised \(2p\) orbital perpendicular to the molecular plane. These two parallel \(p\) orbitals overlap sideways above and below the plane to give the \(\pi\) bond, whereas end-to-end overlap would give a \(\sigma\) bond. Matches option B.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: The \(\sigma\) bond between two carbon atoms in ethane is formed by:
solution: Both carbons in ethane are \(sp^3\) hybridised and the carbon-to-carbon bond comes from head-on, end-to-end overlap of one hybrid orbital from each atom along the internuclear axis. Of the four printed choices only end-to-end overlap describes a \(\sigma\) bond built from \(p\)-derived orbitals. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Strictly the overlap is sp3-sp3 (hybrid orbitals), not pure p-p; the printed option set offers no hybrid-orbital choice, so (D) end-to-end overlap is the intended answer under the usual textbook simplification.

subtopic: Hybridization
stem: Which type of overlap produces a \(\pi\) bond?
solution: A \(\pi\) bond arises when two parallel \(p\) orbitals overlap laterally, above and below the internuclear axis. Head-on and axial overlap both describe the same along-the-axis overlap that produces a \(\sigma\) bond, and spiro overlap is not an overlap type. Matches option B.
